name: Joseph H. Williams Tallgrass Prairie Preserve
blurb: Free-ranging bison, patch-burn fire and the largest tallgrass prairie left.

tip.title: Take away fire
tip.text: Fire clears dead growth, keeps brush out and draws bison to fresh regrowth. Set Fire to -100% and watch the grasses, then the animals that depend on them.

sources.title: The Nature Conservancy: Tallgrass Prairie Preserve

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: A tall warm-season grass that dominates the preserve grasslands alongside switchgrass, reaching 6 to 8 feet by September.

nodes.name: Milkweeds
nodes.desc: Prairie wildflowers whose leaves feed monarch caterpillars and whose flowers feed many insects. Antelope-horns and butterfly milkweed are well recorded here.
Free-ranging herd of roughly 2,500 animals used since 1989 to restore the prairie. Grazing and patch burning together shape the habitat.
Common in the wooded parts of the preserve. Eats leaves, forbs and grasses and is prey for coyotes and bobcats.
A small grass-eating rodent and the most recorded mammal near the preserve. Hawks, harriers and coyotes all take voles.
A common grassland rodent that eats plants and is food for hawks, harriers and coyotes.
Eats grasses and wildflowers including milkweed and is prey for hawks, coyotes and bobcats.
A large grasshopper that chews grasses and forbs and feeds birds such as prairie-chickens.
Caterpillars feed on milkweed; adults sip nectar from prairie flowers. The preserve names monarchs among its highlights.
A threatened grouse that eats seeds, green plants and insects such as grasshoppers. Males boom on open display grounds each spring.
A widespread hawk that hunts rodents and rabbits over open ground. Recorded in GloBI taking voles and cotton rats.
A low-flying hawk of open grassland, common on the preserve in fall and winter, hunting small rodents.
A grassland songbird named among the preserve highlights. Feeds on insects including grasshoppers during the breeding season.
Soars over the prairie and cleans up carcasses of animals such as deer and rabbits.
A top predator of the preserve. GloBI records it eating voles, cotton rats, rabbits and deer.
A secretive wild cat named among the preserve highlights. Hunts rabbits, rodents and sometimes deer.
Warm-season grasses grow fastest in summer heat and long days.
Spring and early summer rain sets how tall the grass grows.
Deep root systems build rich soil and store nutrients under the grass.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and soil invertebrates break down dead grass, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
